rationale: The capture condition r2 && !r1 uses the first synchroniser stage r1 in logic, which is early fan-out that can make the load enable metastable. The capture also fires on the synchronised falling edge of the request, after the source's stated payload-validity window has closed. Both are genuine defects at the same capture.
caveats: The case contains two defects, against the one-defect-per-bad-fixture rule. CDC-007, and CDC-029 if it treats r1 as an under-depth qualifier, detect the early-stage use. No current predicate detects the stability-window violation. CDC-039 is only an obligation and earns no credit. Recommend splitting: a variant using r2 && !r3 with a full chain would isolate the stability-window defect as a bad case with empty expected_rules and a detection_gap.
A CDC-007 hit is credited as detection of a real defect in this case. It does not show that the stability-window defect was found.

Raw rst_n asynchronously resets every register with no local release synchroniser and no SDC reset exception; RDC-003 (WARNING Unresolved), RDC-002 (WARNING Unresolved) and RDC-013 (physical obligation) are expected if RDC rules run. The contract states only asynchronous assertion, so this is a whole-IP premise gap, not a defect of the labelled crossing.
